title: Rows of a tree
description:
A scene is a flat list of objects, each knowing its parent (`-1` for a root). Write the order the tree's rows appear on screen:

```cpp
struct Object { int id; int parent; std::string name; };

std::vector<int> displayOrder(const std::vector<Object>& objects, const std::set<int>& open);
```

- Roots come first-to-last in the order they appear in `objects`; so do the children of each object.
- A row is shown for every root, and for every child of an **open** object whose own row is shown (depth first: an object's children come right after it, before its next sibling).
- Return the ids in row order.

```
objects: 1 "Level" (root), 2 "Props" (parent 1), 3 "Rock" (parent 2), 4 "Lights" (parent 1), 5 "UI" (root)
open {1}      -> 1, 2, 4, 5
open {1, 2}   -> 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
open {2}      -> 1, 5          (2 is open but its parent is closed, so it is not shown)
```
